_comment: Reads Table 12 down the columns: the exposure rate divides by its own column total, and the gap is in percentage points.

stem.en: In Table 12, 33 of the 35 men with lung cancer had smoked, and 55 of the 82 controls had smoked. By how many percentage points do the two exposure rates differ? Give your answer to 1 decimal place.

explanation.en: 33 / 35 = 94.3 per cent and 55 / 82 = 67.1 per cent, so the gap is 27.2 percentage points. The source prints 94.2 and 67.0 after its own rounding, and the gap is the same 27.2. Each rate divides by its own column total, which is what makes the two comparable.

hints.en: Work out each exposure rate with its own column total, then subtract one from the other.
